lawyer:
For the Petitioners : Mr. Ibrahim Khalil, Advocate-on-Record. 
Respondent : Not represented

The State ------ Petitioner

Saber Hossain Chowdhury ------ Respondent
full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Hassan Ameen, J: The petitioner (respondent) seeks leave to appeal against the judgment and order dated 27-04-2005 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.4256 of 2003 making the Rule absolute. 

 2. The prosecution case, in brief, is that the Inspector of Bureau of Anti-Corruption lodged a First Information Report with the Mohammadpur Police Station on 11.12.2001 stating, inter alia, that the Ministry of Local Government, Rural Development and Co-operative allotted 1,18,000 Metric tons of wheat and 30,000 Metric tons of rice in favour of the Chief Engineer of Local Government and Engineering Department for the year 1999-2000 and in the said letter of allotment, it has been mentioned that allotted wheat and rice are to be utilize as per Growth Center Connecting Road (9G.C.C.R.) r Project. After getting allotment the Chief Engineer, re-allotted 1,54,0620.526 Metric tons of wheat and 33,397.67 Metric tons of rice and that have been withdrawn from the Goclown. Mr: Monowar Hossain Chowdhury by misusing his power has allotted excess amount of wheat 18,683.37 Metric tons worth Tk.14,08,79,100 and 3337.37 Metric Tons of rice worth Tk.3,46,53,174 and in this way by re-allotting has caused financial loss to the Government thereby misappropriated the said amount. Mr. Amirul Morshed was the Project Director and in discharging his duty he had not kept the account of the allotted wheat and rice due to his collaboration, scope has been created for re-allotment of excess amount. Mr. Saber Hossain Chowdhury, the Deputy Minister for Hossain Chowdhury (Md. Hassan Ameenj) 67  Local Government and Rural Development and Co-operative passed orders for allotment on receiving application from different persons without being informed about the correct information about project. He has fixed the quantum of re-allotment and the same is an example of misuse of power due to his aforesaid act. The Chief Engineer misappropriated the price allotted for rice and wheat and thus the aforesaid accused committed an offence under sections 409/109 of the Penal Code read with Section 5(2) of Act II of 1947. The Mohammadpur Police Station registered the Case against the petitioner and, others being Mohammadpur Police Station Case 37 dated 11.12.2001. 

 3. The police after investigation submitted charge sheet against the petitioner and two others on 27.10.2002 under sections 409/109 of the Penal Code read with Section 5(2) of the Act No. II of 1947. The case was then transferred to the Divisional Special Judge, Dhaka and the same was registered as Special Case No.107 of 2002. The petitioner thereafter surrendered before the court and was enlarged on bail. The petitioner filed an application under Section 241 A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and that was rejected. The Divisional Special Judge after hearing the parties framed charge under section 5(2) of Act II of 1947 on 02.03.2003. 

 4. Thereafter, the present petitioner (respondent) moved the High Court Division under Section 561A of the Code Criminal Procedure of quashment of the proceeding on the ground that the case under Section 5(2) of the Act II of 1947 does not lie against him (petitioner) and the facts as stated therein does not attract the ingredience of Section 5(2) of Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 and as such the proceeding is an abuse of the process of the Court and is liable to be quashed. 

 5. Mr. Md. Ibrahim Khalil, the Advocate-on-Record appearing for the petitioner, submits that in case of re-allotment of wheat and rice certain procedures are to be followed and the planning and Implementation Method for L.G.E.D. pre-supposed to be followed and in that case the petitioner-respondent did not follow and misuse by re-allotment of excess wheat and rice which is an offence under law. He further submits that the petitioner-respondent having personal gain has convinced the other co-accused and passed such order for re-allotment of excess allotment and thereby he has gained and thus committed an offence under Section 5(2) of Act II of 1947. He further submits that the learned Judges of the High Court Division passed the impugned judgment and order without considering prima-facie case as made out in the First Information Report and the charge sheet, as such the impugned judgment and order is liable to be set aside. He lastly submits that the learned Judges of the High Court Division while entertaining the application under Section 561A of the Code Criminal Procedure did not consider that in the First Information Report and charge sheet submitted by the police there was specific allegations that the accused-respondents had specific involvement of indulging in corrupt practices constituting offence under Section 5(2) of Act II of 1947.
